items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO PROCUREMENT AND CONTRACTS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to posting the names of
individuals who are authorized to sign state contracts and eliminating
unfavorable terms in state contracts
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5304

SPONSOR: REICHLIN-MELNICK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to posting the names
of individuals who are authorized to sign state contracts and eliminat-
ing unfavorable terms in state contracts

 
PURPOSE:

Allows for the authorization of signatories and terms and conditions
that void state contracts

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends § 110 of the state finance law adding subdivision 1-a,
requiring each department that maintains a public website to publicly
post and maintain on that website a list of current names of the indi-
viduals who the department has authorized to execute contracts on behalf
of the department.

Section 2 amends the state finance law by adding section 139-m, provid-
ing that certain terms and conditions in any contract entered into by
the state or any department thereof shall be void and unenforceable.
Such terms and conditions include those
  1. require the state or the department to indemnify or hold harmless
another person, except as otherwise authorized by law;
  2. which purports to reserve a right to the contractor to unilaterally
amend, revise, or add to the terms and conditions without the consent of
the state or the department;
  3. by which the state or the department agrees to limit the liability
of another person for bodily injury, death, or damage to tangible prop-
erty caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of such person; and
  4. that designates the law of another jurisdiction as the law govern-
ing the contract.

Section 3 provides the effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill will increase transparency by requiring each department with a
public website to publicly post and maintain a webpage showing a current
list of individuals authorized to sign state contracts on behalf of each
department. The bill also specifies the types of terms and conditions
that would render a specific contract provision void and unenforceable.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to posting the names of

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5304A

SPONSOR: REICHLIN-MELNICK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to posting the names
of individuals who are authorized to sign state contracts and eliminat-
ing unfavorable terms in state contracts

 
PURPOSE:

Allows for the authorization of signatories and terms and conditions
that void state contracts

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends § 110 of the state finance law adding subdivision 1-a,
requiring each department that maintains a public website to publicly
post and maintain on that website a list of current names of the indi-
viduals who the department has authorized to execute contracts on behalf
of the department.

Section 2 amends the state finance law by adding section 139-m, provid-
ing that certain terms and conditions in any contract entered into by
the state or any department thereof shall be void and unenforceable.
Such terms and conditions include those

1. require the state or the department to indemnify or hold harmless
another person, except as otherwise authorized by law;

2. which purports to reserve a right to the contractor to unilaterally
amend, revise, or add to the terms and conditions without the consent of
the state or the department;

3. by which the state or the department agrees to limit the liability of
another person for bodily injury, death, or damage to tangible property
caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of such person; and

4. that designates the law of another jurisdiction as the law governing
the contract, except for terms and conditions in contracts with another
state or the federal government.

Section 3 provides the effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This proposal was amended to address constitutional concerns related to
language used in section 2 to void any terms and conditions that desig-
nates the laws of a jurisdiction other than NYS as governing the
contract. To address those concerns, the bill now makes an exception for
contracts with another state or the federal government. This bill will
increase transparency by requiring each department with a public website
to publicly post and maintain a webpage showing a current list of indi-
viduals authorized to sign state contracts on behalf of each department.
The bill also specifies the types of terms and conditions that would
render a specific contract provision void and unenforceable.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately
